title: [finding] A model-tier quota limit can block a whole lane — the termination signal, and the "which paths are ACTUALLY mandated" split that keeps work moving
body:
Filed unassigned by the skills execution seat at shift end (session `session_01JANH3y7qe3MD8aLaLXci8N`, 2026-08-26/27). Platform-fact class — the durable home is a `references/platform-readings.md` row, not prose. Grading is the lane's.

## Fact 1 — how a tier-quota death presents, and that it IS a host signal

A dispatched subagent terminated mid-edit with the host reporting the account's `claude-fable-5` limit reached. This is a **host signal**, so it satisfies the standing rule that "maintainer abort" needs an explicit signal while a subagent death is an ordinary death: it is neither. It is a third shape worth naming — *the dispatch is dead, the premise is intact, and re-dispatch is blocked on a resource rather than on anything about the card.* Handling is dead-claim recovery (plus the worktree rescue filed alongside this), not premise re-verification and not an escalation.

⚠️ There is no pre-flight probe: quota state is not observable before dispatch, only when the dev dies inside it. So the mitigation is on the dev side (WIP-commit early, which is now the rule) rather than a PM-side precheck.

## Fact 2 — a mandated tier is not a preference, and the lane is not therefore stopped

The mandated tier must not be downgraded because it is unavailable — that is precisely the substitution the downgrade fuse exists to refuse. But "this lane's work is fable-mandated" is usually **recalled, not derived**, and the recalled version is too wide. Measured today with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier PATH`, per path rather than per lane:

| surface | derived tier |
|:--|:--|
| `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` | **MANDATORY** `claude-fable-5` (clause ①) |
| `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` | no path-derived mandate — floor sonnet · default opus · ceiling fable |
| `references/**` | no path-derived mandate (left the path mandate in the 2026-08-20 narrowing) |

So a blocked fold splits: the instruction-file halves wait for the tier, while reference fact rows and gate-script work dispatch at the default tier immediately. Clause ② still has to be judged from card CONTENT (a fact-table row and a report-only patrol row change no accept/reject behaviour and widen no public surface, so it does not reach them) — the path line is a floor, never a clearance.

**The reusable rule**: when a tier becomes unavailable, ⛔ do not declare the lane blocked from memory — re-derive the mandate per file surface and dispatch the unmandated remainder. Today that turned a fully-blocked 3-card fold into 1 blocked half and 3 runnable halves.

Live instance carrying both facts: #12220 (recovery record + the split), with #12200 / #12286 as the split members.
